Your day, understood.

Suzzme lives on your iPhone and turns the context you choose to share into a calm view of what matters. Ask it anything about your day, and it helps you act.

See how it works

From scattered context to a clear next step.

  1. Only what you permit

    Calendar, Reminders, Contacts and public pages you choose to watch. Nothing is read behind your back.

  2. Understood in context

    Events, deadlines and changes are connected with today and with memory you can inspect, then ranked by what matters now.

  3. Then something useful happens

    Suzzme reminds, summarizes, answers or acts. When nothing needs you, it stays quiet.

One request, followed all the way through.

On iPhone, your words, the context they touch and the decision they need stay together, from the first word to a verified result.

  1. 1

    Ask the way you would ask a person.

    Talk or type. Both start the same request session, and speaking never gets more authority than typing.

  2. 2

    Find the exact thing you meant.

    Suzzme grounds the request in Calendar context you permitted and resolves one specific event and time.

  3. 3

    See the change before it happens.

    The action and its target stay on screen. Nothing changes until you confirm.

  4. 4

    Done means checked.

    Deterministic Swift performs the change, reads Calendar again, and only then tells you it’s finished.

On your Mac, it lives just below the notch.

Listening. Suzzme is hearing your request.

Privacy isn’t a setting. It’s how Suzzme behaves.

On-device first

Apple Foundation Models run locally where available. Personal context isn’t a prompt to hand away.

Memory you can inspect

See what Suzzme remembers and where it came from. Correct it or delete it whenever you like.

Honest when things are missing

When a source or advanced model is unavailable, Suzzme says so plainly instead of filling the gap.

Things Suzzme will never do

  • Read your Messages or WhatsApp
  • Scrape your notifications
  • Open another app’s private database
  • Use private Apple APIs
  • Draw a fake Dynamic Island
  • Say “done” before checking it’s done

Run it from source today.

Suzzme isn’t publicly distributed yet. The shared SwiftUI target runs on an iPhone simulator or on your Mac.

Grant only the permissions you choose. Everything else keeps working.

Questions, answered plainly.

What is Suzzme?

A privacy-first personal intelligence layer, built for iPhone first and also available on Mac. It explains your day, keeps useful memory, answers questions and safely performs supported actions.

Which sources can it use?

Calendar, Reminders, Contacts and public webpages you explicitly choose to watch. What’s available depends on the current build and the permissions you grant.

Can it act without asking?

No. Language models may understand and propose. Deterministic Swift code owns permission, confirmation when required, execution and verification.

Does it use the Dynamic Island?

No. On iPhone, Suzzme stays inside its own app and never draws a fake island. On MacBooks with a notch, Presence is an app-owned surface just below the notch, built with public APIs.

When can I use it?

Suzzme is in development. You can build it from source now, or join the waitlist to hear when a public build is ready.

Who is building Suzzme?

Dhanesh Shetty and Rehan.
